items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: I was hiring people like Sidney Bechet and Muggsy Spanier, you know, for my regular concerts.

ctx.x: And it was a black theater and I used to come out of, out of class and go across the street to the theater all the time, because I knew a lot of the musicians that were, that were playing in the, in the show. And it was during the time when I had first started doing jazz concerts. So it was 1936 and I went backstage, because his band was playing there. And I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there, Al Nicholas. So, I had, I had met Louis before, I don't actually remember when, but…
Okay, we're on the second reel. Al Rose, same date. August 13th, 1989. Okay, we left off with Eus... Eus Panassia.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: But frequently, and maybe usually, when I hired Sidney for a job, I'd also hire a clarinet player who played mainly the ensemble parts.

ctx.x: I find it very difficult to think of many trumpet players that really suited his clarinet playing, specifically I'm speaking.

Well, I found that Max Kaminsky worked out very well with Sidney. And at that time, most of the people that wanted to hear Sidney were really interested in hearing him play Summertime on the fish horn. And we're not very discriminating about bands anyway. It seemed like I was the only one who was worried about the sound of the band. But frequently, and maybe usually, when I hired Sidney for a job, I'd also hire a clarinet player who played mainly the ensemble parts. And it was not uncommon for me to have both…
That worked certainly. Let's see. We were talking about recording sessions. It was Joe Maera- Mm-hm. He worked with him. Were you working for Joe Maera- Mm-hm.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: I knew him well, and I did a lot of concerts with him, and we traveled together, but I never made a record.

ctx.x: And you've done stuff with Sidney Bache quite a bit, I would say.

I never recorded Sidney Bache. Oh, you never did record him? No. I knew him well, and I did a lot of concerts with him, and we traveled together, but I never made a record. No, you never made a record. No. Chips never fell that way. Okay. We must be to the end.
